title: Compound nouns 1: noun + noun
subtitle: credit card, blood pressure, traffic lights
summary: Understand and use compound nouns made of two nouns, and learn how they are written, stressed and counted.

lesson.heading: What are compound nouns?
lesson.text: A compound noun is a fixed expression made up of more than one word which works as a single noun. Very often it is two nouns together. If you understand both parts, the meaning is usually clear.

examples.text: a **car park** - a park for cars
**science fiction** - fiction based on some kind of scientific fantasy
a **tin opener** - an opener for tins; a **bank account** - an account in a bank

lesson.heading: How are they written?
rows: tin opener, bank account, pedestrian crossing, alarm clock
lesson.note: There are no strict rules about which way a compound noun is written - even dictionaries disagree. A trademark is the symbol of a product; a babysitter stays with a child while the parents are out.

lesson.heading: Stress in compound nouns
lesson.text: Usually the main stress falls on the first part of the compound, but sometimes on the second. It is worth marking the stress when you record a new compound noun.

examples.text: stress on the first part: an **alarm** clock, a **blood** donor, a **burglar** alarm, a **bus** stop, a **credit** card, a **light** bulb, a **tea** bag
stress on the second part: a heart **attack**, a package **holiday**, a steering **wheel**, a youth **hostel**, mineral **water**
more compounds to learn: a **contact lens**, a **windscreen wiper**, **voice mail**

lesson.heading: Uncountable compound nouns
rows: blood pressure, food poisoning, hay fever, junk food
air traffic control, computer technology, data processing, mail order
birth control, income tax, pocket money
lesson.note: Hay fever is an allergy to pollen. These nouns have no plural: we say *some cotton wool*, not ~~two cotton wools~~.

left.label: Used only in the singular
examples: the **arms race** - two or more countries competing to have the most powerful military
the **labour force**, the **sound barrier**, the **welfare state**

lesson.heading: Working out the meaning
lesson.text: Ask yourself what the first noun tells you about the second. That usually explains the whole compound.

examples.text: a **windscreen** is a screen that protects a driver from the wind
a **burglar alarm** is an alarm in a house which goes off if burglars try to get in
**pocket money** is small amounts of money to spend as you wish, usually given by parents to children
the **welfare state** is the part of the state that provides welfare for the members of society who need it

lesson.text: One element can build several compounds. From *blood*: blood pressure, blood donor, blood ties. From *control*: air traffic control, birth control, self-control.

exercises.prompt: Which network does each compound noun belong to?
Match each compound noun with its explanation.

pairs.right: an alarm that goes off if someone breaks into a house
the difficulty parents and children have in understanding each other
things that are luxuries rather than necessities
the part of the state that supports those in need

exercises.prompt: I had it taken at the doctor's this morning and he said it was a little high for my age. He was talking about my ___.
exercises.explanation: Blood pressure is an uncountable compound noun.

exercises.prompt: It's happening through man-made pollution and is causing more extreme weather. This is ___.
exercises.explanation: Climate change is used only in the singular.

exercises.prompt: She always has terrible sneezing fits in the early summer. She suffers from ___.
I can't understand why countries spend so much on devising ways of killing people. It's the ___.
exercises.explanation: The arms race is countries competing to have the most powerful military.

exercises.prompt: They say that working there is much more stressful than being a pilot. The job is ___.
exercises.explanation: Air traffic control is an uncountable compound noun.

exercises.prompt: The worst time was when one fell out at the theatre and I spent the interval searching on the floor. I can't see a thing without them. They are ___.
exercises.explanation: A contact lens is a countable compound noun.

exercises.prompt: I don't think it should ever be used, whatever the crime. This is the ___.
exercises.explanation: The death penalty is used only in the singular.

exercises.prompt: It's much easier not to have to make your own travel arrangements, so we booked a ___.
exercises.explanation: On a package holiday, travel and accommodation are arranged for you.

exercises.prompt: You really shouldn't cross the road at any other place. Use the ___.
exercises.explanation: A pedestrian crossing is a place for people to cross a road.

exercises.prompt: I had it very badly once when I ate some chicken that wasn't properly cooked. It was ___.
exercises.explanation: Food poisoning means being made ill by food you have eaten.

exercises.prompt: 'I didn't like the low-energy ones at first because they're so slow to get going.' What are they?
exercises.explanation: Low-energy light bulbs take a while to reach full brightness.

exercises.prompt: Complete the compound noun: junk ___ and junk ___ (unwanted post; unhealthy food).
exercises.explanation: Junk mail is unwanted advertising post; junk food is unhealthy processed food.

exercises.prompt: Complete each compound noun with the right second element.
Is each compound noun used only in the singular or only in the plural?

exercises.statement: A windscreen is a screen that protects the driver from the wind.
exercises.explanation: Correct - the first noun tells you what the second one is for or against.
